main_text.p:
Novi vitam meam, à Malitia Diaboli, & impiorum hominum unicum jam diu scopum peti, esse tamen sub Dei custodia, cui, non ideo ut vitam longiorem eblandiar, sic Me volo ostendere paratum mori, sed ab Ipso humiliter pendere cupio, & Me totum Illius voluntati tum in Vita tum in Morte (quocunque eas ordine dispensare placuerit) submittere. Arduum fateor negotium tot diversis Mortis horroribus (queis Me Deus tentari permittit) sed pari omnibus atrocitate conflictari, dum vel furores cogitem repentinæ trucidationis: vel illas Iudiciorum Formas, quas forsan Hostes mei (non secus ac Illi Christi interfectores) sunt usurpaturi, ut solennmore[?] quadam truculentia per hæc Justitiæ ludibria Malitiam suam confummeant: quod tamen astu necessario ideo forsan sunt facturi, ut hæc Pompa percuntis minus mei misereantur homines, in quem ut Noxium animadverti ex Jure credent (Principem videlicet à Subditis!) Ipsi interim non ignorantes nullam Divinam aut Humanam Legem hoc Illis concedere, ut sine Me in quempiam alium, nedum in Me quicquam statuant, quique omnibus Sacris (coram Deo & hominibus) vinculis Me tueri obligati, jam Perjurium suum quæ
runt hoc Iustitiæ pallio obtegere.
Misera sane conditio, ut quis Hostes suos habeat Accusatores, Actores, Iudices, sed illa omnium deploratissima, ut hæc Subditorum insolentia in Regem audeat, eorumque qui rei

page.notes: Page numeral "252" and running head read from a slightly faded scan; the running head is in Greek capitals. "solennmore" is a doubtful reading (possibly "solenniore") and is marked [?]. The word "Perjurium" in the first paragraph was split across a line break, shown as "quæ/runt"; the join is a transcription artifact and should be restored as "quærunt". The margin shows only bleed-through from the facing page, which is not transcribed. Italic words were judged from the letterforms and may be partly inexact.
